solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: On air row traumatised and exhausted Robert Plant (9)

indicatorNotes.traumatised: a row shaken up so badly its letters are thrown about
indicatorNotes.exhausted: Robert emptied of everything but his outer letters

blocks.note: a programme on air is live
anagram fodder
RoberT with its contents used up, leaving the outer letters
anagram indicator for ROW and RT together

annotation.surface: A broadcast quarrel leaves the Led Zeppelin singer Robert Plant shaken and worn out.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface borrows the rock singer Robert Plant; split the name and 'Plant' alone is the definition, with 'Robert' feeding the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A liverwort is a small, flat, moss-like green plant.

entries.clue: Substitute officer upset uniform men at the start (5)

indicatorNotes.upset: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down, so it reads upwards
indicatorNotes.at the start: only the opening letter of men is taken

blocks.note: COL, short for colonel, turned over
U is Uniform in the NATO alphabet
the first letter of Men

annotation.surface: An officer is annoyed that the men turned up in the wrong uniform at the start of the day.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reads as the officer's mood; in a down clue it flips COL so it reads upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor or cleric standing in for another: a substitute.

entries.clue: Sweet eclair Calvin ordered each month (7,3,5)

indicatorNotes.ordered: the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters
ea. is the abbreviation for each
m. is the abbreviation for month
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Someone called Calvin orders an eclair every month as his treat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' reads as buying from a shop, which suits the eclair; it is the signal to rearrange. In Britain a sweet is also a dessert course.
annotation.definitionFit: Vanilla ice cream is a dessert, and a sweet is the British word for the dessert course.

entries.clue: Staggers after receiving shock treatment, puts back in power (2-6)

indicatorNotes.after receiving: the staggers word takes something inside it

blocks.note: to reel is to stagger
ECT, electroconvulsive therapy, placed inside REEL…S

annotation.surface: A patient totters about after electric shock therapy.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pulls 'shock treatment' and 'power' into one medical-electrical picture; 'power' is political, and ECT is the standard abbreviation for electroconvulsive therapy.
annotation.definitionFit: To re-elect is to vote someone back into office.

entries.clue: Served up spirit, just missing king … sorry! (4)

indicatorNotes.Served up: in a down clue, served up means presented upwards, so the word runs bottom to top
indicatorNotes.just missing: the king falls away, leaving the rest

blocks.note: a spook is a ghost; turned upwards it reads KOOPS
KOOPS loses K, the chess abbreviation for king

annotation.surface: A waiter who serves the spirits apologises for having just missed the king.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' next to 'served up' suggests a drink poured; it is a ghost.
annotation.definitionFit: Oops is the exclamation of a person owning up to a small blunder, much like sorry.

entries.clue: Grotty old vagrant last seen in cave? (10)

annotation.definition: Grotty old vagrant last seen in cave?

indicatorNotes.vagrant: wandering, so the letters drift out of place
indicatorNotes.last seen in: only what is seen last in the next word, its final letter

blocks.note: anagram fodder
the last letter of cavE
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A scruffy old tramp was last spotted sheltering in a cave.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: it is the wordplay, and it is also a fair picture of a troglodyte.
annotation.definitionFit: A troglodyte is a cave dweller, and by extension a rough, backward person.

entries.clue: Piercing, principally shrill instrument (5)

indicatorNotes.principally: take the principal, that is the first, letter

blocks.note: the first letter of Shrill
a harp is a musical instrument

annotation.surface: A shrill, piercing instrument, like a whistle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Piercing' and 'shrill' look like two descriptions of the same noise; only 'Piercing' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Sharp and piercing both describe a point, a pain or a sound.

entries.clue: Way to accommodate long bag (6)

indicatorNotes.to accommodate: the way word finds room inside itself for the other

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street
to long for something is to ache for it; placed inside S…T

annotation.surface: A long bag that needs a way of fitting in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Long' sits beside 'bag' like an adjective; it is the verb, to yearn.
annotation.definitionFit: A sachet is a small sealed bag of powder or liquid.

entries.clue: Cameramen used at broadcast games screened here (9,6)

indicatorNotes.broadcast: scattered widely, as seed is broadcast

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: TV camera crews working at a televised sports event.
annotation.walkthrough: Cameramen, broadcast and screened all belong to television sport; the games are video games shown on arcade machine screens.
annotation.definitionFit: An amusement arcade is full of video games played on screens.

entries.clue: Post Office worker struggling to pen book, one written to raise cash (9)

indicatorNotes.to pen: to pen is to shut in, as sheep in a pen

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation
one who toils, labouring hard
b. is the abbreviation for book; it goes inside T…OILER

annotation.surface: A postal worker labours to write a book to make some money.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like writing, which suits the surface exactly; here it means enclose.
annotation.definitionFit: A potboiler is a book or artwork churned out simply to earn a living, to keep the pot boiling.

entries.clue: Smashing racket crime? (8,2,5)

blocks.note: the surface pushes an organised scam; the setter means a tennis player hurling a racket down on the court
the question mark flags that this offence is committed against a tennis court, not a court of law

annotation.surface: A tennis player in a tantrum breaks a racket.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Racket' suggests an organised criminal scheme next to 'crime'; it is a tennis racket, and the court is the tennis court rather than the law court.
annotation.definitionFit: Contempt of court is the offence of disrespecting or defying a court of law.

entries.clue: Disease from beer we knocked back (6)

indicatorNotes.knocked back: knocked backwards, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: mild is a dark, lightly hopped British beer
WE turned round

annotation.surface: An illness caught from the beer we drank.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' is drinking slang for downing a pint, which fits the beer; here it turns WE around.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: mildew is a fungus that attacks plants, one kind of plant disease.

entries.clue: Imperative to get little George a close friend (5,3)

blocks.note: the answer, read as a command, is an anagram instruction whose result is GEO, the short form of George
the straight definition

annotation.surface: An urgent need to find a young George a best friend.
annotation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: ALTER EGO read as a command says rearrange EGO, and doing so gives GEO, little George. The clue states the result, not the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: An alter ego is a second self, hence a trusted, intimate friend.

entries.clue: Plucky wife, endlessly zealous officer in reserve (4,6)

indicatorNotes.endlessly: without an end, so the word's final letter is cut off

blocks.note: game means willing and spirited
w. is the abbreviation for wife
ARDENT without its last letter

annotation.surface: A brave wife is married to an ever-keen army reservist.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' suggests reserve soldiers; it is a nature or game reserve.
annotation.definitionFit: A game warden polices a game reserve, protecting its wildlife.

entries.clue: Huge letters used to spell “Dad”, being popular in China (5,5)

blocks.note: giant = huge
Dad is PA, whose letters are P and A: P AND A

annotation.surface: Giant characters spelling out 'Dad' prove popular in China.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Being' is the noun, a creature, not a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: The giant panda is China's best-loved animal and national emblem.

entries.clue: Young man’s backing good quality statesman (9)

blocks.note: g = good
a lad's, set behind the G
tone = a quality, as of a sound or voice

annotation.surface: A young man supports a statesman of good character.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Backing' tempts a reversal; here it means supporting from behind, so LAD'S follows G.
annotation.definitionFit: William Gladstone was four times British Prime Minister.

entries.clue: Knock down chap emitting cry of pain (4)

indicatorNotes.emitting: letting out, so the cry leaves the word

blocks.note: a fellow is a chap
ow! is a cry of pain; it comes off the end of the chap word

annotation.surface: A man is knocked down and yells in pain.
annotation.walkthrough: The chap lets out his cry, and FELLOW without OW is FELL; the surface makes emitting sound like shouting.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: felling a tree or a boxer means knocking it to the ground.

entries.clue: Deceitful character put up motorway notice (8)

indicatorNotes.put up: in a down clue, put up means raised, so the word reads upwards

blocks.note: the M1, Britain's first motorway, written as M1 and read upwards
a poster is a notice put up on a wall

annotation.surface: A con man erects a fake road sign on the motorway.
annotation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; the digit 1 stands in for the letter I.
annotation.definitionFit: An imposter pretends to be someone else to deceive.

entries.clue: Chief taking off first of the month (4)

blocks.note: March is a month
MARCH without its first letter M

annotation.surface: The boss takes the first of the month off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The month' is one particular month; the crossing letters show it is March.
annotation.definitionFit: Arch means chief or principal, as in arch-enemy or archbishop.

entries.clue: Write uninspiring incomplete ending for literary work (10)

annotation.definitionNote: a pentameter is a line of verse, a loose sense of work

indicatorNotes.incomplete: the word is not finished, losing its last letter

blocks.note: to pen is to write
tame = dull, uninspiring
TERM, an end, without its last letter

annotation.surface: Advice to an author to write a dull, unfinished ending for a novel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ending for' reads as the close of the book; ending gives TERM, and 'for' only links to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A pentameter is a line of verse with five metrical feet, the stuff of literary work.

entries.clue: Plastic factory beginning to implement cuts (6)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: only the first letter of implement
indicatorNotes.cuts: the letter cuts into the factory word

blocks.note: a plant is a factory
the first letter of Implement, set inside PL…ANT

annotation.surface: A plastics factory is starting to put job cuts into effect.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plastic factory' reads as one noun phrase; 'Plastic' alone is the definition, an adjective meaning bendable.
annotation.definitionFit: Plastic in its older sense means easily shaped, as pliant does.

entries.clue: Italian snail unexpectedly seen around here in France (8)

indicatorNotes.unexpectedly: the snail's letters turn up in an unexpected order
indicatorNotes.seen around: the rearranged snail wraps around the French word

blocks.note: SNAIL rearranged
ici is French for here, placed after the S

annotation.surface: An Italian is surprised to spot a snail near here while in France.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Italian' is the definition; the answer names someone from one region, Sicily.
annotation.definitionFit: A Sicilian is from Sicily, part of Italy, so an Italian.

entries.clue: Husky is a cracking four-legged friend (6)

indicatorNotes.cracking: the A breaks into the other word

blocks.note: the article as printed
a horse, with A inside HO…RSE

annotation.surface: A husky dog is a brilliant four-legged friend.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Husky' looks like the sled dog, and 'cracking' like praise; the husky is a rough voice.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a voice made rough and low by a sore throat.

entries.clue: Lament English cricket side, the ultimate in ignominy (5)

indicatorNotes.the ultimate in: the final letter of the next word

blocks.note: E = English
the leg side is the half of a cricket field behind the batsman's legs
the last letter of ignominY

annotation.surface: Grief over the English cricket team's final disgrace.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Side' reads as a team; in cricket it is also half of the field, leg side and off side.
annotation.definitionFit: An elegy is a poem or song of mourning, a lament.

entries.clue: Congress supporting leaders of White House a tiny bit (4)

indicatorNotes.supporting: in a down clue, a supporting word sits underneath
indicatorNotes.leaders of: the first letters of the words that follow

blocks.note: the first letters of White and House
congress = sex, and it is a coy word for sex

annotation.surface: The US Congress backs the President's leadership just a little.
annotation.walkthrough: Congress and the White House are a political pair; here congress is sexual intercourse, and 'it' is a crossword staple for that.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, now heard mostly in the idiom 'not a whit', meaning not at all.

entries.clue: Inspector isn’t overworked by this perfunctory luggage check? (4-3-4,4)

blocks.note: a police inspector's easy case, solved at once
a suitcase opened and shut straight away by a customs inspector

annotation.surface: A customs inspector gives the bags a lazy glance.
annotation.walkthrough: The inspector is both a detective and a customs officer, and the case both a crime and a suitcase.
annotation.definitionFit: An open-and-shut case is one so clear it is resolved with no effort.

entries.clue: This compiler heading west bumped into tourist (5)

indicatorNotes.heading west: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left

blocks.note: the setter speaking of himself
to bump into someone is to meet them

annotation.surface: The setter, travelling west, ran into a holidaymaker.
annotation.walkthrough: Emmet is Cornish slang for a tourist, from an old word for ant; heading west to Cornwall is where one meets them.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: Cornish locals call summer visitors emmets, their dialect word for ants.

entries.clue: Turned on Conservative about regular instances of vilest infamy (9)

indicatorNotes.Turned: turned as a coat or a page is, so the word faces the other way
indicatorNotes.about: the Tory goes around the other letters
indicatorNotes.regular instances of: letters recurring at a regular interval, here every second one

blocks.note: ON reversed
a Tory is a British Conservative
the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of vIlEsT, placed inside TOR…Y

annotation.surface: A Conservative scandal about the vilest disgrace sets everyone off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turned on' reads as switched on or excited; it is ON turned round.
annotation.definitionFit: Notoriety is fame for something bad, which is infamy.
